title: Python for Data Scientists
tagline: From EDA to models that predict — and explanations stakeholders can use
description: A three-level Python curriculum for Data Scientists. pandas and statistics first, then scikit-learn modeling, then evaluation, fairness, and monitoring so models survive contact with the real world.
prerequisites: Python basics (or complete the analyst Python foundations in parallel)
High-school algebra; willingness to relearn probability in context
A public dataset you care about (finance, health, or operations)

levels.title: Quantitative Python Foundations
levels.goal: Clean data, explore it honestly, and state a question a model could answer

topics.title: Statistics refresher
items: Hypothesis testing at a working level

topics.title: Exploratory analysis
items: Leakage, target definition, and train/test splits

topics.title: Feature engineering
items: Writing features so they can be rebuilt in production later

projects: EDA notebook on a public dataset with a written question
Baseline descriptive model of churn, default, or demand

levels.title: Machine Learning Core
levels.goal: Train, evaluate, and explain supervised models without fooling yourself

topics.title: Regression & classification
items: Trees, ensembles, and when they help
Cross-validation that respects time or groups

projects: End-to-end classifier or regressor with a held-out test
Credit/churn/collections model framed for a SACCO or fintech stakeholder

levels.title: Models in the Real World
levels.goal: Ship models with monitoring, fairness checks, and a clear recommendation

topics.title: Fairness & drift
items: Bias checks on protected and proxy attributes

projects: End-to-end model on a real or public dataset with documented limitations
Monitoring sketch: what to watch in production
Recommendation memo: ship, iterate, or stop
